item.title: Physics-Informed Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Applications
item.content:encoded:
Jiangbei Hu, Dalian University of Technology

Ben Fei, The Chinese University of Hong Kong

Yajun Cao, Hangzhou Dianzi University

This special issue addresses the integration of physical laws and mathematical structures into AI models for engineering systems. The challenge of creating accurate and generalizable AI systems in complex operating conditions motivates the inclusion of domain knowledge directly into learning architectures, combining data-driven approaches with established engineering principles.

item.title: Physical Machine Learning and Large Language Models for Remote Sensing and Earth Observation
item.content:encoded:
Wenchao Zhang, Xi'an University of Science and Technology

Yongze Song, Curtin University

Jiaxin Li, Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

Remote sensing and Earth observation are advancing through integration of multi-source satellite and UAV data with machine learning and large language models. Physical machine learning—combining physics knowledge with data-driven approaches through physics-informed constraints and neural operators—enhances consistency and generalization. Geospatial foundation models and multimodal language systems enable knowledge transfer across sensors and support open-vocabulary perception and reasoning.

This special issue seeks original research on physics-informed learning, geospatial foundation models, and language-based intelligence for remote sensing applications. Submissions should advance methodological approaches, establish benchmarks, or demonstrate applications that improve accuracy, generalization, interpretability, and operational value across environmental monitoring, resource management, and disaster response. Studies combining these complementary approaches are particularly encouraged.

item.title: Operational Research and Artificial Intelligence for Transforming Healthcare
item.content:encoded:
Adele Marshall, Queen's University Belfast

Laura Boyle, Queen's University Belfast

Sally Brailsford, University of Southampton

Erwin Hans, University of Twente

Brian Denton, University of Michigan

Martin Kunc, University of Southampton

Healthcare systems globally face mounting challenges from aging populations and workforce constraints while simultaneously benefiting from expanding digital health data and artificial intelligence capabilities. This special issue explores how Operational Research and AI methods can be combined to improve healthcare planning, delivery, and evaluation. Building on prior work examining the OR-AI interface, this collection focuses specifically on healthcare applications where reliable and verifiable AI is critical.

The special issue seeks original research demonstrating substantive contributions at the intersection of OR and AI in healthcare contexts. Submissions should include methodological advances, applied studies with measurable practical value, and work addressing real-world implementation challenges. Papers focused solely on optimization or simulation without significant AI integration may be more appropriate for other venues.

Appel publié par Journal of the Operational Research Society. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Machine learning and predictive modelling for patient flow, demand forecasting, and clinical decision support integrated with OR
  • Large language models, generative AI, and retrieval-augmented generation for extracting modelling insight from unstructured clinical documents and health records
  • Reinforcement learning and approximate dynamic programming for sequential decisions in screening, treatment, and care planning
  • Generative approaches to synthetic health data for modelling and privacy-preserving analysis
  • Optimisation of healthcare resources including workforce planning, scheduling, and capacity management using integrated AI and OR methodologies
  • Hybrid simulation–AI approaches for the design and evaluation of care delivery
  • Data-driven and digital-twin models of care pathways and healthcare delivery
  • Statistical and stochastic modelling of patient journeys and survival
  • AI-enhanced planning and delivery of care in emergency, unscheduled, and elective settings
  • Personalised and stratified care through AI-enabled pathways, screening, prevention, and chronic disease management

item.title: Forecasting for a Sustainable Future: Energy Systems, Climate Risks, Environmental Governance, Financial Markets and Societal Resilience
item.content:encoded:
Goutte Stephane, Université Paris Saclay

This special issue addresses the fragmentation between environmental sciences, energy systems, public health, and finance by promoting integrated forecasting methodologies capable of anticipating cascading systemic risks. Research communities need to develop common predictive frameworks that capture complex feedback mechanisms linking environmental governance, ecosystem services, financial markets and societal resilience under unprecedented uncertainty.

The special issue welcomes innovations in econometric, statistical, machine learning and artificial intelligence approaches using novel data sources such as satellite imagery and alternative data. Key focus areas include electricity system resilience under renewable integration, carbon market forecasting, natural capital accounting, sustainable finance, and the distributional impacts of energy transitions.

Contributions are sought globally with emphasis on emerging and developing economies perspectives. The collection will comprise 10-12 peer-reviewed articles demonstrating methodological diversity and practical relevance for policymakers, regulators, investors and sustainability managers.

Appel publié par Journal of Forecasting. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: AI in the Built Environment: Opportunities, Risks, and Future Directions
item.content:encoded:
Sara Wilkinson, University of Technology Sydney

Johnny Wong, University of Technology Sydney

Biyanka Ekanayake, University of Technology Sydney

This special issue examines how artificial intelligence is transforming the built environment across construction, real estate, facilities management, and urban planning. While AI technologies offer significant opportunities for innovation and efficiency through applications like energy optimization, smart building control, and predictive maintenance, the sector faces critical challenges regarding data integrity, algorithmic bias, privacy, and transparent decision-making.

The special issue seeks high-quality original research exploring AI's use, impact, risks, and future potential in the built environment. It welcomes contributions spanning construction automation, property valuation, smart buildings, urban planning, generative design, AI governance and ethics, sustainability applications, security systems, human-AI collaboration, and professional education in AI.

Appel publié par Building Research & Information. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • AI in construction: automation, robotics, quality control, progress monitoring, risk and safety analytics
  • AI in property and real estate: valuation models, market intelligence, customer engagement, asset management, predictive analytics
  • Smart buildings and facilities management: IoT-enabled optimisation, energy management, predictive maintenance, AI-driven knowledge systems
  • AI in urban planning and infrastructure: spatial modelling, forecasting, environmental assessment, transport and mobility analytics
  • Design and engineering applications: generative design, simulation, optimisation, digital twins, parametric modelling
  • Explainable AI (XAI): AI governance, ethics, and regulation: transparency, bias, data integrity, privacy, and responsible GenAI in the built environment
  • AI for sustainability and ESG: carbon modelling, resource optimisation, lifecycle assessment
  • Security and risk management: computer vision for surveillance, access control, anomaly detection
  • Multimodal and agentic AI: advanced AI systems applied to complex built environment challenges
  • Human-AI collaboration: professional adoption, skills, workflows, and organisational change
  • The challenge of educating and training built environment professionals in AI

item.title: Advanced Machine Learning for System Reliability Management
item.content:encoded:
Yan-Fu Li, Tsinghua University

Hoang Pham, Rutgers University

Xu-Feng Zhao, Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

Industrial systems produce vast sensor-generated datasets that strain computational resources. Advanced machine learning techniques including transfer learning, federated learning, quantum machine learning, and reinforcement learning provide scalable solutions for handling large data volumes and enabling informed decision-making. Recent applications of these techniques to system reliability management encompass fault diagnosis, health assessment, remaining useful life prediction, degradation analysis, and maintenance optimization. This special issue seeks original research papers, reviews, and case studies exploring these emerging applications.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Machine learning-enhanced maintenance optimization

  • Reinforcement learning for maintenance decision making
  • Transfer learning for cross-domain maintenance
  • Generative models for synthetic data generation for predictive maintenance
  • Self-supervised learning for unlabeled data for fault detection
  • Large models for fault detection and/or diagnosis
  • Generative models for reliability testing
  • Meta-heuristics for large-scale reliability design optimization

item.title: Advances in Reliability and Statistical Computing for Intelligent Systems
item.content:encoded:
This special issue addresses advances in reliability and statistical computing for intelligent systems, reflecting the significant developments in AI and machine learning applications. The call seeks research that combines theoretical rigor with practical relevance, particularly focusing on how intelligent systems can provide reliable and timely responses in real-world applications across service industries and everyday use.

The special issue welcomes papers on new theoretical research and computational methods that advance the field. Preference is given to contributions demonstrating practical applications over purely theoretical work, with industrial case studies especially valued across domains such as robotics, medical care, education, surveillance, and intelligent transportation systems.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Climate Transition and Operational Risk Modelling: Implications for Supply Chains and Financial Decision-Making
item.content:encoded:
This special issue addresses how climate-related risks disrupt interconnected financial and economic systems during the transition to a low-carbon economy. The challenge lies in modeling how transition risks affect firms and supply chains, particularly carbon-intensive sectors, and understanding risk transmission across economic systems.

Firms face competing pressures to decarbonize while maintaining profitability and competitiveness. Significant vulnerabilities emerge through supply chain interdependencies, where disruptions propagate and amplify operational risks. The call seeks integrated modeling approaches that capture emissions, disruptions, and risks across supply chain tiers using operations research methods.

The issue welcomes applied and methodological studies employing stochastic optimization, machine learning, and other advanced techniques to examine how financial institutions manage uncertainty in portfolio allocation and risk management under climate transition scenarios.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Robust stochastic optimization methods for climate transition risks
  • Portfolio optimization and risk-adjusted return modelling under climate policy uncertainty
  • Credit and counterparty risk assessment under low-carbon transition scenarios
  • Risk-sharing mechanisms and insurance models for climate-related disruptions
  • Supply chain risk management in climate transition
  • Operational decision-making in emission trading schemes and carbon pricing
  • Predictive modelling of carbon stranding risk via supervised learning
  • Machine learning and big data analytics for climate risk scenario classification
  • Natural language processing applications in climate policy risk analysis
  • Bayesian network approaches to modelling climate transition risk propagation
  • Agent-based models of climate transition dynamics and systemic effects

item.title: Collaborative Intelligence in Operations Research: Models, Methods, and Applications
item.content:encoded:
Olga Battaïa, Kedge Business School

Yasser Dessouky, San Jose State University

Reza Zanjirani Farahani, Paris School of Business

Masood Fathi, University of Skövde

Madjid Tavana, La Salle University

Modern operations research faces challenges in dynamic and uncertain environments where traditional methodologies struggle. This special issue focuses on Collaborative Intelligence—integrating human expertise, artificial intelligence, and distributed problem-solving to enhance adaptability and efficiency in complex operations through multi-agent coordination, human-AI collaboration, and machine learning.

The special issue seeks research bridging autonomous AI systems and human decision-makers by combining computational power with human intuition and ethical reasoning. Contributions should address how collaborative approaches improve system resilience, handle uncertainty, and increase trust in AI-driven systems through theoretical advancements and computational methods that extend operations research to adaptive and multi-agent frameworks.

Researchers are invited to submit original contributions involving innovative mathematical models, algorithms, and practical applications demonstrating how collaborative intelligence enhances decision-making in complex operational environments, balancing theoretical rigor with practical relevance.

item.title: Contextual Optimization with Side Information: Theory, Methodology, and Applications
item.content:encoded:
Modern operations research increasingly relies on contextual information to enhance decision-making in uncertain environments. This special issue focuses on the integration of side information—such as demand patterns, user behaviors, and market conditions—into optimization models to achieve more adaptive and data-driven policies. The field spans contextual stochastic optimization, distributionally robust optimization with covariates, decision-focused learning, and online optimization frameworks.

Real-world applications present significant challenges including high-dimensional data, noisy observations, distribution shifts, computational constraints, and the need to balance predictive accuracy with operational performance. The special issue seeks high-quality contributions that develop novel theories, algorithms, and applications combining optimization with machine learning, statistics, and data analytics to address these challenges systematically.

item.title: Data-Driven Reliability Modeling and Decision Support in Industrial Engineering Systems
item.content:encoded:
Industrial engineering systems such as manufacturing, supply chains, energy networks, and transportation require reliable operation to maintain efficiency and safety amid uncertainty and disruptions. Traditional reliability approaches have relied on probabilistic and stochastic analysis, but advances in sensing technology and data collection now enable data-driven reliability modeling that combines classical theory with machine learning and statistical methods. The field is increasingly focused on integrating reliability analysis into decision-making frameworks for maintenance planning, resource allocation, and system optimization.

This special issue invites original research papers addressing reliability modeling and decision support for industrial engineering systems using operations research, industrial engineering, and data-driven methods. Both theoretical contributions and practical applications are welcome, with emphasis on methodological rigor and real-world relevance.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Innovations in Production Planning: Emerging Problems and Modern Solution Paradigms
item.content:encoded:
Mirco Peron, NEOMA Business School

Ibrahim Kucukkoc, Balikesir University

Daniel Alejandro Rossit, Universidad Nacional del Sur

Ilkyeong Moon, Seoul National University

Olga Battaïa, KEDGE Business School

Michael Pinedo, Stern School of Business, New York University

Production planning has long been central to operations management, with classical problems like scheduling and capacity planning addressed through mathematical programming and heuristics. However, emerging technologies—cyber-physical systems, IoT, digital twins, additive manufacturing, and AI—are fundamentally transforming both the problems planners face and the methods available to solve them.

These technological shifts have introduced new planning challenges: digital twin-driven real-time optimization, hybrid conventional-additive manufacturing systems, reconfigurable production topologies, circular economy objectives, and resilience under global disruptions. Concurrently, solution approaches have evolved from traditional optimization to data-driven methods including reinforcement learning, hybrid metaheuristics, simulation-optimization frameworks, and multi-agent systems.

Appel publié par International Journal of Production Research. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Evolution of classical planning problems (lot sizing, capacity planning, scheduling, assembly line balancing) in modern manufacturing contexts
  • Planning in reconfigurable, modular, and hybrid manufacturing systems
  • Integration of additive manufacturing and conventional processes in planning
  • Additive manufacturing production scheduling
  • Digital twin–enabled planning and real-time adaptive scheduling
  • Production planning under sustainability, circular economy, emissions or carbon goals
  • Resilience-oriented planning under uncertainty, disruptions, and volatility
  • Advanced optimization methods: decomposition, robust/stochastic models, metaheuristics
  • Machine learning, reinforcement learning, hybrid AI–optimization for planning
  • Simulation–optimization frameworks and surrogate modeling
  • Production Planning problems associated with customized environments (engineering-to-order, make-to-order, mass customization)
  • Human–robot collaborative systems and operator-driven planning in the context of Industry 5.0
  • Reinforcement learning / deep learning models applied to dynamic planning and scheduling, (e.g., graph neural network and RL architectures for scheduling problems)
  • Optimization of production and inventory strategies in modern distribution systems (e.g., e-commerce, platform-based logistics)

item.title: Theorizing the Data-AI Nexus
item.content:encoded:
Cristina Alaimo, ESSEC Business School

Lauren Waardenburg, ESSEC Business School

Jonny Holmström, Umeå University

Lior Zalmanson, Tel Aviv University

Reza M. Baygi, VU Amsterdam

The special issue addresses a fundamental shift in how artificial intelligence operates: contemporary AI systems are built upon, learn from, and generate data at scale, making data rather than rules the core substrate of computational intelligence. This requires Information Systems scholars to develop new conceptual frameworks for understanding the data-AI nexus as a socio-technical phenomenon, moving beyond purely technical perspectives.

The call emphasizes that data are shaped by institutional practices and cognitive frames, while AI systems increasingly reshape the data they depend on, blurring boundaries between data and AI. Practitioners primarily engage with AI through data practices such as curation, labelling, and quality control, making it essential to understand the organizational routines and historical infrastructures that underpin these processes. Additionally, AI now generates synthetic data that feeds back into model training, raising institutional and epistemic challenges.

Appel publié par European Journal of Information Systems. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Data and AI co-constitution: exploring where intelligence emerges in computational architectures, datasets, or their entanglement; how data selection, curation, labelling, and historical accumulation shape AI capabilities
  • AI as a data-maker: conceptualizing AI as an active producer of data; how classification systems, predictive models, and generative tools reorganize reality; AI agents autonomously generating and acting upon data; recursive dynamics of synthetic data training other AI systems
  • Data decoupled from practice: consequences of data production detached from institutionalized knowledge practices; governance and decision-making based on decontextualized data; risks when data-driven systems lack ties to local knowledge and professional judgment
  • The social life of the data-AI nexus: institutional, historical, and cognitive trajectories of data; how organizational memory, institutional logics, and collective sensemaking shape datasets and AI output interpretation; AI agents as new organizational actors
  • Theoretical and methodological discussions: analyses of co-constitution, entanglement, flow, recursion, performativity, and classification; reconceptualizing constructs like intelligence, data quality, ground truth, and model performance as relational and emergent
  • Cross-level insights: how assumptions about data and intelligence are embedded in AI systems; studies of data work (curation, labelling, cleaning), model development, synthetic data pipelines, generative AI integration
  • Data, AI and grand challenges: addressing climate change, public health, inequality, and geopolitical tensions; responsible AI design with incomplete, biased, or synthetic data; governance and accountability in distinctive contexts (scientific, environmental, planetary)
